citation: Aerospace PO terms (contract); supports the customer's own FAR 52.204-21 and CMMC duties
trigger: A cyber incident that affects, or may affect, the customer's information (drawings are FCI) on shop systems
notify: Aerospace customer buyer and its security contact (named on the PO terms)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contract term on every aerospace PO

obligation: OEM notice of unauthorized access to confidential information
trigger: Unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, an OEM's drawings, models, or specifications
deadline: Within 5 business days (two SQAs); the third OEM's NDA says promptly, so use the same 5 days

obligation: OEM notice before shipping parts whose program integrity is unconfirmed
citation: OEM SQAs (change control and nonconforming product terms; contract)
trigger: Any released program that may have been altered or restored from an unverified copy
deadline: Before shipment; hold affected lots. The OEM then decides whether its own FDA duties (21 CFR 803 or 806) are triggered; those duties are the OEM's, not the shop's

obligation: DoD cyber incident report for covered defense information
trigger: Cyber incident affecting covered defense information
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery; preserve images 90 days
notify: DoD via https://dibnet.dod.mil (subcontractors also give the incident number to the prime)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the shop holds no covered defense information and the clause is not flowed down. If CUI is found on shop systems, tell the aerospace customer the same day and follow its instructions

obligation: CMMC Level 1 status after an incident
trigger: The incident shows that a Level 1 requirement is no longer MET
deadline: Before the next affirmation, and before claiming a current status on any award
notify: Correct the gap, re-run the self-assessment, and update SPRS; tell the aerospace customer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes once the shop holds a Level 1 (Self) status. Author reading: a status is current only while there are no changes in compliance since the status date

citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (flowed down under 52.204-25(e)); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered telecommunications equipment or services found during contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; mitigation details within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: The aerospace customer, which reports to its contracting officer or https://dibnet.dod.mil
applies_at_this_tier: Only if found; machined parts contain no telecommunications equipment

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (name plus SSN, license, financial account, or medical data; or a username or email with its password)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - the shop holds no personal information of other individuals; customer contacts are business names and emails. Confirm during scoping

trigger: Personal information of residents of other states affected
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - same reason; check if any personal data is found

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Strict liability; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement or CISA
